Local heritage. New perspectives.
01 / The research

One place.
A more connected
heritage experience.

Heritage information, educational materials, immersive exploration, and visitor services serve different needs. When they are spread across separate channels, visitors can struggle to connect discovery with meaningful learning, while staff face additional content-management work.

This study addresses the need for an integrated, site-specific platform that brings these experiences together for visitors, learners, community members, and museum personnel.

The general objective

To design, develop, test, and evaluate a WebXR-enabled digital heritage platform that supports accessible, interactive, and immersive heritage learning for onsite and offsite users.

Four objectives. One integrated platform.

  1. Design an integrated experience

    Bring curated heritage information, bilingual content, inclusive access, and appropriately scoped immersive experiences into one web platform.

  2. Develop the identified modules

    Implement heritage and educational content, immersive experiences, accessibility support, visitor services, and administrative management.

  3. Test the system’s functions

    Check the major public and administrative features against specified requirements through documented black-box test cases.

  4. Evaluate the user experience

    Assess user acceptance, perceived usefulness, ease of use, immersive experience, accessibility, and related evaluation criteria.

04 / Research methodology

Built in iterations.
Informed by people.

Descriptive, developmental, and evaluative research

The study connected museum needs with system design, implementation, functional testing, and a descriptive evaluation of users’ experiences.

Requirements grounded in the museumInterviews, onsite observations, document examination, and consultation with museum personnel informed content, accessibility, and service requirements.

An iterative Agile development modelSix phases supported repeated review and refinement. Feedback could lead the team back to an earlier phase.

Two different forms of assessmentBlack-box testing checked specified functions. User evaluation described respondents’ perceptions and acceptance after interacting with the system.

The development cycle

Planning

Identify stakeholder needs, available heritage content, intended users, project scope, and functional requirements.

Design

Plan the information architecture, interface, database, navigation, workflows, accessibility mechanisms, and immersive interactions.

Development

Build and integrate public and administrative modules, multimedia, accounts, visitor services, and selected immersive experiences incrementally.

Testing

Conduct internal checks and documented black-box tests. Address identified issues and retest affected functions where needed.

Deployment

Make the working platform available for intended use and evaluation within the capstone’s scope. The application uses Python/Flask on Vercel with Supabase database and storage services.

Feedback & refinement

Review observations and evaluation findings, assess feasible recommendations, and revise the relevant system components.

Select a phase to read what the researchers did.

05 / Reported study findings

Tested functions.
Documented experiences.

The supplied manuscript reports the following results for the tested and evaluated version of the platform.

54 / 54
Functional test cases passed

Across 13 module or feature groups, under the documented testing conditions.

190
Completed user evaluations

Respondents assessed the platform through a five-point questionnaire.

4.77 / 5
Overall weighted mean

Interpreted as “Strongly Agree” in the study’s evaluation scale.

Source: supplied manuscript, abstract and Chapter IV, including Table 4.21. These are reported research results, rather than live website analytics or a claim that every possible device and usage condition has been tested.

Explore the eight user-evaluation criteria
All eight criteria were interpreted as “Strongly Agree” in the manuscript.
Evaluation criterionWeighted mean / 5
Selected Software Quality Characteristics4.82
Perceived Ease of Use4.73
Perceived Usefulness4.84
Attitude Toward Using4.83
Behavioral Intention to Use4.82
Actual System Interaction4.67
Immersive Digital Experience4.73
Accessibility4.72

Scope and limitations. The project covers selected heritage materials and supported visitor services. Immersive experiences depend on connectivity, permissions, and device capabilities. Perceived accessibility is distinct from formal accessibility conformance, and the evaluation does not establish long-term adoption or measured learning gains.
